articles.title: I removed the account wall from checkout. The 48-hour claim link is where the risk lives.
articles.excerpt: For a year my checkout had a wall in front of it: an account was required before payment. The reasoning was simple — a subscription has to belong to somebody. The cost was less simple. People who had…
articles.body: For a year my checkout had a wall in front of it: an account was required before payment. The reasoning was simple — a subscription has to belong to somebody. The cost was less simple. People who had already decided to buy were asked to invent a password first, and some of them left at exactly that moment. The most expensive step of a funnel is the step that asks for something other than money. So I removed the wall. Anyone can now complete a purchase with nothing but an email address. This post is about the second half of that change, which is the part that actually matters: after the money arrives, how does the buyer get the workspace? Two halves, and only one of them is easy Half one is checkout.
articles.author: 付小花

articles.title: Your AI agent writes Playwright tests that pass while your API returns 500
articles.excerpt: AI agents now write a lot of Playwright tests. You ask Claude Code or Copilot to "add a test for the checkout", or let an agent explore your app through Playwright MCP and turn what it did into a spec…
articles.body: AI agents now write a lot of Playwright tests. You ask Claude Code or Copilot to "add a test for the checkout", or let an agent explore your app through Playwright MCP and turn what it did into a spec. Healer agents even fix failing tests for you. Here is the kind of test they write: import { test , expect } from " @playwright/test " ; test ( " places an order " , async ({ page }) => { await page . goto ( " / " ); await page . getByLabel ( " Name " ). fill ( " Ada " ); await page . getByRole ( " button " , { name : " Place order " }). click (); await expect ( page . getByRole ( " status " )). toContainText ( " Order placed " ); }); It's a good test: role-based locators and a web-first assertion. It passes.

articles.title: DoorDash Has Seen Hundreds of AI-Agent Orders. Build a Checkout That Knows When to Stop
articles.excerpt: A shopping agent can find a restaurant, assemble a cart, and call an ordering API. The hard question comes one step later: when is it allowed to spend the user's money? DoorDash's latest earnings disc…
articles.body: A shopping agent can find a restaurant, assemble a cart, and call an ordering API. The hard question comes one step later: when is it allowed to spend the user's money? DoorDash's latest earnings discussion offers a useful reality check. CEO Tony Xu said the company had seen “maybe several hundred orders in total” from some third-party AI agents. That is a cumulative count for those agents, not all orders and not a quarterly total. The same report says customers still predominantly order through DoorDash's own app. The company has also built its own agent experiences and an MCP connector for corporate ordering. The signal is not that agents cannot order. It is that connecting an agent to a real fulfillment network does not automatically make people use it.

articles.title: LedgerGuard: Investigating the Ghost in Financial Transactions
articles.excerpt: Financial discrepancies are not always obvious. A payment may be allocated to the wrong invoice, a delivery may not match an order, or records across different systems may contradict each other. I bui…
articles.body: Financial discrepancies are not always obvious. A payment may be allocated to the wrong invoice, a delivery may not match an order, or records across different systems may contradict each other. I built LedgerGuard , an AI-powered financial reconciliation and investigation platform, for the Hacktoberfest 2026 DEV Challenge — Week 4: Ghost in the Machine. What does LedgerGuard do? LedgerGuard combines deterministic reconciliation with AI-assisted investigation to help identify and understand inconsistencies across business records. Key capabilities include: Reconciliation engine: Detects quantity, operational, and financial discrepancies. Cross-record checks: Identifies suspicious relationships between deliveries, invoices, and payments.
articles.author: Hibat Errahmane Gholal

articles.title: My model router taught me that 'frontier' is a marketing tier, not a quality guarantee
articles.excerpt: I spent weeks assuming that picking the biggest model was the safe move. Then I actually measured it. I run a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint that routes across 50+ models with auto/eco/premium tier…
articles.body: I spent weeks assuming that picking the biggest model was the safe move. Then I actually measured it. I run a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint that routes across 50+ models with auto/eco/premium tiers, and the first thing the logs showed me was that agents don't need the biggest model — they need the right one. A classification task that cost $0.08 on a frontier model cost $0.002 on a mid-tier one with identical accuracy on my eval set. The frontier model wasn't better; it was just more expensive at being the same. The second lesson: latency matters more than agents admit. A 4-second response on a premium model breaks a tool-calling loop that a 900ms eco-tier response sails through.

articles.excerpt: Project Name: Echoes of the Ofrenda (Ecos de la Ofrenda) Project Overview How It Works Voice Capture: A family member speaks into the mic, sharing unscripted memories, stories, or anecdotes about a lo…
articles.body: Project Name: Echoes of the Ofrenda (Ecos de la Ofrenda)  Project Overview Echoes of the Ofrenda is a fully local, privacy-first oral history and digital ofrenda builder designed to honor ancestors for Día de los Muertos. The application runs entirely on a laptop without an internet connection. It records spoken family stories, transcribes them using an open-source speech-to-text model, and utilizes a local open-weight Large Language Model (LLM) to extract memories, favorite foods, songs, and distinct traits of departed loved ones.

articles.title: Ghostlight: Don't Recreate the Person. Preserve the Moments.
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine Some of the most important things a family knows are never written down. They live in stories told duri…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 4: Ghost in the Machine What I Built Some of the most important things a family knows are never written down. They live in stories told during a festival, recipes explained while someone is cooking, journeys remembered years later, and small details that only one person knows. Sometimes those stories exist as voice notes on a phone. Sometimes they exist only in someone's memory. When that person is no longer around to tell the story, finding and preserving those details becomes difficult. The obvious AI solution would be to build a chatbot that pretends to be that person. I didn't want to do that.

articles.body: Yesterday, news broke that Sir Patrick Stewart died at age 86. With his background performing Shakespeare and his incredible sense of dignity and gravitas, Stewart is being celebrated primarily for his work as Captain Jean-Luc Picard on Star Trek: The Next Generation , as well as being the perfect man to portray Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films. But while he was beloved for the dramatic weight he brought to his roles, it's worth acknowledging that the man pulled off some incredibly memorable comedic performances, one of the first was on The Simpsons , where he guest-starred in the season 6 episode, “Homer the Great.”

articles.body: If you’re playing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 on Nintendo Switch 2, beware: you’re at a disadvantage in competitive Multiplayer due to crushing input lag that is much worse than the other platforms. Digital Foundry’s analysis of the performance of the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 — the first Call of Duty released on a Nintendo console since 2013’s Ghosts — found that the input lag on Switch 2 can be two times longer than on PS5 at 60fps. articles.excerpt: Anakin Skywalker actor Hayden Christensen has revealed the strangest fan encounter he’s ever had.
articles.body: Anakin Skywalker actor Hayden Christensen has revealed the strangest fan encounter he’s ever had. Speaking on stage at L.A. Comic Con, as reported by The Nerd Wire , the Star Wars veteran said that years ago, a burglar recognized him during a robbery at his home, apologized, then gave his stuff back. Christensen was upstairs when he heard the door open, and when he found the burglar, he was holding his belongings. “I’m like, is this a delivery guy?” Christensen was quoted as saying. “And I look and I’m like, this is all my stuff.” Remarkably, Christensen then offered to buy the man who broke into his house a train ticket home. No, a Jedi mind trick hadn’t caused the burglar to have a surprise change of heart. He just happened to be a fan who decided on a quick U-turn.

articles.body: On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
articles.excerpt: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. Here's why it was so creepy.
articles.body: On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images.

articles.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
articles.excerpt: The waning moon shines with Jupiter, Mars and the brilliant star Regulus in the eastern sky overnight Nov. 1-2.
articles.body: The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer .

articles.title: Betelgeuse is haunted by a cosmic poltergeist tormenting the doomed star's atmosphere
articles.excerpt: Radio images show the supergiant's atmosphere recovering from its dramatic dimming, while a companion plows through its outer layers.
articles.body: Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant. New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
articles.author: Dan Goodin
